records.title: A Test for Superior Predictive Ability
records.analyst_paraphrase: The SPA framework tests whether any member of a declared model family improves expected loss over a benchmark while accounting for comparison across models, under explicit dependence/asymptotic assumptions.

verification.publication_status: Peer-reviewed Journal of Business & Economic Statistics 23(4), 365–380 (2005)
verification.read_depth: Fetched abstract and index-extracted original published text, including pages 365–366 estimation/stationarity limitations. Direct publisher open failed; mirror PDF timed out. Proof/bootstrap implementation not fully reviewed.
verification.critical_applicability_limit: Original framework excludes recursively re-estimated parameters; fixed conditional and rolling schemes are discussed. Do not apply unchanged to expanding-window refits.
verification.hypothesis_limit: Omnibus rejection concerns some improvement within the declared family; it does not identify a uniquely best model or guarantee future performance.

policy: Preserve identities, metadata, search ranks, dated provider citation counts and analyst paraphrases only. No full abstracts/snippets. Citation counts are provider snapshots and popularity signals, not quality scores. Every cited search result is fetched first; primary source verification and read depth are separate.
findings: Treat cross-sectional factor pricing, realized-return co-movement and per-asset forecasting as distinct claims.
Investigate dated-futures basis as a later controlled ablation, with horizon, roll/unit and joint availability policies; do not equate with perpetual funding.
Keep strong GBM baselines and admit a pinned TabPFN-2 challenger only after rights/runtime/PIT qualification; neither generic benchmark chooses the financial winner.
LLM text features need model-version/time provenance, identifier-masking controls and fresh forward evaluation.
Statistical test admission must match estimation scheme; original 2005 SPA is not a default for recursive/expanding refits.
